from z3 import *

def solve_bibd(v, b, r, k, lam):
    X = [[Bool(f"x_{i}_{j}") for j in range(b)] for i in range(v)]
    s = Solver()
    
    # Each column has exactly k ones
    for j in range(b):
        s.add(PbEq([(X[i][j], 1) for i in range(v)], k))
        
    # Each row has exactly r ones
    for i in range(v):
        s.add(PbEq([(X[i][j], 1) for j in range(b)], r))
        
    # Any two rows have exactly lam ones in common
    for i1 in range(v):
        for i2 in range(i1 + 1, v):
            s.add(PbEq([(And(X[i1][j], X[i2][j]), 1) for j in range(b)], lam))
            
    # Symmetry breaking
    # Sort columns lexicographically
    for j in range(b - 1):
        # X[][j] >= X[][j+1]
        # We can just do a simple lexicographical order
        conds = []
        for i in range(v):
            # if all previous are equal, then X[i][j] >= X[i][j+1]
            eqs = [X[i2][j] == X[i2][j+1] for i2 in range(i)]
            conds.append(Implies(And(eqs) if eqs else True, X[i][j] >= X[i][j+1]))
        s.add(And(conds))
        
    print("Solving...")
    if s.check() == sat:
        m = s.model()
        res = [[1 if is_true(m[X[i][j]]) else 0 for j in range(b)] for i in range(v)]
        print("SAT")
        print(res)
    else:
        print("UNSAT")

solve_bibd(10, 30, 9, 3, 2)
